gen-dafont-azonix-lora: Lora is a classic serif with a welcoming c and hairline thinning only where its curves turn, bookish and warm. Azonix, wide and rigid, gives it a stiff, commanding header to lean against.
gen-dafont-azonix-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads like a literary page with a gentle thick-and-thin pulse and a big x-height. Azonix does its best work being wide and uniformly stroked, while the serif simply carries the sentences.
gen-dafont-bebas-kai-fs-literata: Bebas Kai crowds its letters into a compact, high-waisted line, every stroke pressed with the same weight. Literata loosens things below with sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier stems, and curves that stay open.
gen-dafont-berylium-fs-bespoke-serif: Berylium draws smooth, minimal letters with one unbroken line weight and a g and s that curl wide open. Bespoke Serif, a classic serif with thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, adds dignity underneath.
gen-dafont-biko-fs-bespoke-serif: A big visible entrance into every curve gives Biko a cozy, hand-led character, with a weight that never wavers. And Bespoke Serif does the dignified work, its thin strokes a touch lighter than its thick ones.
gen-dafont-blockletter-lora: Lora reads literary and bookish, its curves swelling slightly like a reed pen and its c opening broadly. Blockletter sits above it, precise and unvarying, with a tall midsection.
gen-dafont-blockletter-noto-serif: Blockletter draws precise, modern shapes with a tall midsection and no stress in any curve. Noto Serif, a classic serif, handles the quieter job with a faint swell in each curve, like pulled taffy.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-gambetta: Bloody is all commanding display, with big round lowercase bowls that dominate a line. Gambetta, a text serif with wide channels into each counter and graceful shifting weight, is the graceful half of the pair.
gen-dafont-bloody-lora: Commanding is how Bloody lands, with big round lowercase bowls and almost no stroke contrast. Lora, a text serif, brings a mild, approachable contrast and a broad c, which makes the pair feel bookish.
gen-dafont-bloody-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads universal and literary, with a prominent x-height and a subtle thick-and-thin cadence. Bloody does its best work with big round lowercase bowls and flat weight, while the serif varies its strokes gently.
